data: Eight-cluster Saturn I/IB booster engine — the F-1 rehearsal
Engine registry (PRD-032). Public-source nominal specs; NASA imagery.
Eight engines, eight missions — the Saturn I workhorse

The H-1 was the engine Rocketdyne built to bridge the gap between early ballistic-missile powerplants and the F-1 that would follow. Running a gas-generator cycle on LOX and RP-1, eight H-1s clustered together formed Saturn I's first stage — and later Saturn IB's — flying every unmanned Apollo hardware test and crewed Apollo 7. Its first flight was 27 October 1961; it ran continuously through the end of the Saturn IB program in 1975.
